t: Newly unified Italy's late bid for colonies, spanning Eritrea, Somaliland, Libya, the Dodecanese and, briefly, Ethiopia.
Under Mussolini it became a vehicle for Fascist dreams of a new Roman empire, enforced with poison gas, camps and racial laws.
It collapsed within three years in the Second World War, and the 1947 Treaty of Paris formally stripped Italy of its colonies.
dyk: In 1938 Governor Italo Balbo oversaw the arrival in Libya of some twenty thousand Italian settlers in a single state-organised convoy.
ev: The Italian government takes over Assab Bay on the Red Sea, its first colonial foothold
The colony of Eritrea is formally proclaimed
Menelik II routs General Baratieri's army at Adwa
The Italo-Turkish War begins, bringing coastal Libya and the Dodecanese under Italian control
Libyan resistance leader Omar Mukhtar is executed
Mussolini proclaims the empire after Addis Ababa falls; Africa Orientale Italiana is formed
British and Commonwealth forces end Italian rule in East Africa; Haile Selassie returns
The Allies invade Sicily; Mussolini is dismissed and Italy signs an armistice
